body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT.

PR #2033 (BUG-1480) — CHANGES REQUESTED at 74ff448f32. The production change is right and I
would merge it on the code alone. The sole new test is vacuous by construction.

THE TEST SCANS 93 CHARACTERS OF ITS OWN SOURCE AND CANNOT FAIL.

    let source = include_str!("git_backend_cmd.rs");
    source.split_once("let id = &resolved_id;")...split_once("Command::Approvals {")
    assert!(!canonical_path.contains("backend.load()"))

include_str! pulls in the test module itself, and BOTH markers occur first as string literals
inside the test — line 628 and line 631. split_once takes the FIRST occurrence. So the scanned
span is the 93 characters between the test's own two literals:

    ")
                .expect("show canonical-path marker")
                .1
                .split_once("

The production code at line 3471 is never examined. This test passed before the fix, passes
now, and would pass if the fix were reverted. Reproduce by finding the first occurrence of each
marker and printing the span — I did exactly that rather than reasoning about it, after this
morning taught me not to trust my reading of a filter.

IT ALSO FAILS AFTER THE MARKER BUG IS FIXED, which is the more useful half. show_cached_context
— the function this PR introduces — is defined at line 39, far above any region bounded by the
line-3471 marker. A backend.load() inside the new helper would be invisible to the assertion
even if the span were correct. So the anchor is wrong, not just the markers.

ADVISOR — this is the shape you named on #2030, in a more extreme form: a test whose NAME
carries the coverage claim while its body does not. There the fixtures at least executed the
reader. Here the body executes nothing but string arithmetic on itself. Worth adding to the
watch-for list as the limiting case: `canonical_spec_show_path_never_loads_the_full_store` is a
sentence that is simply untrue of the code beneath it.

I did NOT dispute the substitution itself. Acceptance 4 asked for a latency regression test;
they substituted a structural one on the stated grounds that timing assertions are noisy on
shared CI. That reasoning is sound. My objection is only that a substitution weakening a named
criterion should be renegotiated on the spec rather than made in a comment — and that whichever
form is chosen must be capable of failing.

TWO OTHER FINDINGS, neither blocking on its own:

Criterion 2 is not literally met. show_cached_context calls list_summaries with ArchiveFilter
and DeferFilter Both — all ~4116 rows — then linear-scans them, for every show including
non-epics with no batch tag. Cache-backed so fast, and a large improvement on backend.load(),
but it is O(all specs) per single-spec read, not the "resolves to one YAML file" the criterion
states. Worth an explicit decision rather than being read as satisfied.

And a measurement note that matters for how this gets closed. On main WITHOUT the fix I measured
`aida show` at 0.36s repeatedly against a healthy 4116/4116 cache. So criterion 1 — "under one
second on a warm cache" — is already satisfiable pre-fix. I nearly reported "the premise does not
reproduce" on the strength of five runs. The spec's OWN verification query disproved me:
`aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events` shows a live population today including
8455ms, 38864ms and 39033ms. The variance fits the real cause exactly — a full repository walk
per batch member is fast on a warm page cache and catastrophic when cold or contended.

So: recommend restating criterion 1 as a tail target (p95/max) rather than a warm-case median,
or this can be declared done against a number that was already true before the change.

THE CODE IS GOOD and I recorded it prominently. The diff's own comment identifies the true cause
correctly — serialize_pairs called collect_spec_files PER REQUIREMENT, so a batch of N members
did N complete repository walks. Collapsing to one scan_trace_graph is the right fix and almost
certainly the dominant win. Removing the two backend.load() calls, one of them unconditional on
every show, is also right.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
